title: Plugging in a USB headset causes half its notification sound effect to play on the previous and current output
line: Plugging in a USB headset now plays the device-added sound on the headset instead of starting it on the previous output.
explanation: The devicenotifications kded module sent the "USB Device Detected" notification, and so its sound, the moment udev reported the USB device, before the sound card existed and the sound server had switched the default output to it. The sound therefore started on the previous output and was moved or cut off when the headset became the default. For USB devices that have an audio interface (ID_USB_INTERFACES contains class 01) the notification is now sent two seconds later, so it plays on the new output; other USB devices still notify immediately. If the device is unplugged or another one replaces the notification within those two seconds, the pending one is dropped.

commits.message:
devicenotifications: Delay the notification for USB audio devices

The sound played as soon as the device appeared, before the new output
was ready, so it started on the previous output and was cut off there.
Now it waits two seconds for audio devices, then plays on the new one.

BUG: 517925

media.caption: Master: monitor recordings of both outputs during a fake USB headset plug. The sound starts on the previous output (Speakers) and is cut off when the headset output appears; nothing plays on the headset
With the fix, same plug: the whole sound plays on the headset, about two seconds after plugging, nothing on Speakers
Master: the USB Device Detected popup, shown right away
With the fix: the same popup still appears, two seconds after plugging
